chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a man who was a thief (nabbash). The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) took him by his hair and struck his head against the ground. Then he ordered the people, and they trampled him until he died.

key_terms.نَبَّاش: A specific type of thief, often one who steals from graves or breaks into houses

ai.seo_question: How was the punishment for a thief (nabbash) carried out by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the severity of the *hadd* punishment for *nabbash* (grave robbers) under Imam Ali’s (AS) governance, emphasizing the physical immediacy of the penalty. The act of striking the head against the ground and subsequent trampling by the crowd reflects the public and decisive nature of justice in early Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from mere imprisonment or fines. It underscores the Imam’s personal authority in enforcing divine law with tangible, deterrent force.
